The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has said that the deep depression over East central and adjoining Southeast Bay of Bengal has moved southeastwards and intensified into a Deep Depression today. IMD added that the deep depression is very likely to move nearly southwestwards, and intensify further into a cyclonic storm over east central adjoining Southeast Bay of Bengal by early morning tomorrow. It has advised fishermen not to venture into West Central and adjoining Northwest and Southwest Bay of Bengal during the next two days.The Weather Agency has issued an orange colour warning for heavy to very heavy rainfall over Kerala, Mahe, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal tomorrow. Heavy Rainfall is also expected over Coastal Andhra Pradesh during the next two days.The Met Department has predictedthunderstormsaccompanied by lightning and gusty winds over Gangetic West Bengal, Kerala, Mahe, Lakshadweep and Andaman and Nicobar Islands during the next two to three days.For Delhi, the IMD has forecast a clear sky tomorrow. The maximum temperature in the National Capital will be around 31 to 33 degrees Celsius, while the minimum temperature will hover around 15 to 17 degrees Celsius tomorrow.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has completed 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives. Today, in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into action through initiatives like GST Council.Introduced on 1STJuly, 2017, the Goods and Services Tax (GST) marked a significant milestone in India’s tax reform journey. By bringing multiple Central and State taxes under a unified framework, GST gave effect to the principle of One Nation, One Tax and paved the way for a more integrated and streamlined taxation system across the country. The proposals of the GST Council seek to create a more predictable and taxpayer-friendly GST registration framework. Under the next-generation GST reforms last year, the GST council had simplified the earlier four-tier structure of 5 per cent, 12 percent, 18 percent, 28 percent into a two tier structure of 5 percent and 18 percent. Addressing the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi today, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said that through GST, the government has transformed a complex web of taxes into a national market.Addressing media after the 58thGST Council meeting in New Delhi, Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said that the Council   recommended removing arrest powers under GST, raising the prosecution threshold from one crore to five crore rupees.Over the past nine years, standardised procedures and rationalised rates have supported greater transparency, accountability and economic growth and strengthened the vision of ‘Ek Bharat – Shreshtha Bharat’.

The National Testing Agency (NTA) has extended the last date to submit the online application form for the University Grants Commission National Eligibility Test (UGC NET) December 2026 examination. NTA said that the last date to submit the online application and pay the exam fee is now 31st October. Eligible candidates can apply online without paying any late fee for Junior Research Fellowship (JRF), Assistant Professorship, or PhD through the official website ugcnet.nta.nic.in.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has completed 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives. Today, in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into action through initiatives like Jan Bhagidari.Jan Bhagidari, which means public participation, is a core governance model under Narendra Modi government. Schemes that utilize the Jan Bhagidari model include Swachh Bharat  Mission, Catch the Rain, Vocal for Local, and Pradhan Mantri TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyan. Citizens in India had traditionally been treated as passive beneficiaries of government schemes. Jan Bhagidari has brought a change to this and fostered local ownership and behavioural change in people. Prime Minister Narendra Modi regularly highlights Jan Bhagidari as a core pillar of nation-building through his monthly radio program, Mann Ki Baat. In Mann Ki Baat  last month, Prime Minister Modi again highlighted Jan Bhagidari as a driving force for social change, urging citizens to join collective movements like the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan.Talking to Akashvani News, Shivendra Singh, a resident of Prayagraj, spoke about how he and his family and friends believe in Jan Bhagidari and go Vocal For Local during festive seasons.Participation has now become ownership of transformation happening around the country, with the people becoming stakeholders in national development.

. Global crude oil prices fell today. Brent crude was trading one per cent down at 114 US dollars and 63 cents per barrel. West Texas Intermediate crude was trading 0.8 per cent lower at 100 US dollars and 94 cents per barrel, at the time of writing this report.

. The government today launched the sixth edition of the National Startup Awards to recognise outstanding startups across the country. The awards recognise not just commercial success but also social impact, sustainability, and scalability. Launching the awards in New Delhi today, DPIIT Secretary Amardeep Singh said that startups can apply under 20 sectoral categories. He said that in addition, there are three special categories for women, students, and the North Eastern region. He added that the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade is at the forefront of driving reforms to promote startups. Mr Singh also emphasised the need for more private initiative to bring more startups in the country. He expressed hope that the awards would further boost the startup ecosystem in the country. The Secretary highlighted that the award covers a wide range of domains including agriculture, fintech, aerospace, health, education, and accessibility, among others. The applications for the award will remain open until 20 November this year.In line with the Government’s vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat and the goal of a five-trillion-dollar economy, Startup India supports startups through initiatives such as startup recognition, tax exemptions, regulatory ease, funding access, and capacity building. Launched in 2016, Startup India has transformed India’s entrepreneurial landscape, fostering innovation and empowering youth, women, students, and first-time founders, particularly from Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities. Over two lakh 25 thousand startups have been recognised by DPIIT so far.

India is showcasing its growing capabilities in artificial intelligence, enterprise automation, AI computing infrastructure, cybersecurity, computer vision and intelligent digital solutions at the Dubai AI Festival 2026. The two-day festival, being held on 26-27 October at the Dubai World Trade Centre, focuses on the thematic idea of “Where Intelligence Meets Opportunity”. It brings together technology companies, investors, policymakers and industry leaders to discuss the development and adoption of artificial intelligence. The event is organised by Dubai AI Campus – a business and tech incubator initiative of the Dubai International Financial Centre (DIFC), in partnership with the UAE Minister of State for Artificial Intelligence, Digital Economy and Remote Work Applications. This is the 3rd edition of the event, and the programme covers AI governance, enterprise transformation, computing infrastructure, investment, ethics and the application of AI across sectors.At the Bharat Pavilion, 23 Indian companies are presenting solutions spanning the entire gamut of the AI value chain, from cloud and GPU infrastructure required to train and deploy models to applications designed for specific industries. The pavilion was inaugurated by the Consul General of India in Dubai Dr. Dr. E. Vishnu Vardhan Reddy, on Monday.The showcase includes AI-ready computing infrastructure, GPU cloud services, data-centre capabilities and enterprise cloud management platforms. Indian exhibitors expressed confidence that the solutions they have developed in India have strong potential for deployment in other countries as well. They see the Dubai AI Festival as an important platform to connect with potential clients and partners, expand their global reach and take their technologies to newer markets.As Indian technology companies seek to expand their global footprint and explore new business partnerships, the festival offers Indian companies opportunities to project their capabilities for markets beyond India.

Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal has said, India is open to Chinese suppliers to meet its growing import needs, but will take action through established legal procedures if any unfair pricing is detected. Mr Goyal stated this while talking to reporters in The Hague during his two-day official visit to the Netherlands. He expressed hope that India will emerge as a major exporter to China and the ASEAN region in the coming years. He stressed that India believes in free and fair trade with all countries.The Commerce and Industry Ministry said India also wants greater access to international markets for its goods and services on a reciprocal basis. He expressed confidence that India would become a major exporter to China and Southeast Asian countries in the years ahead. His remarks come amid a significant rise in bilateral trade between India and China.According to the Commerce Ministry, bilateral trade between the two countries rose by around 29 per cent to 91.76 billion US dollars during April to September of the current financial year, making China India’s largest trading partner in the first half of 2026-27.Meanwhile, Mr Goyal said India would work to address the impact of China’s new export controls on key machinery, including tunnel boring machines

The Embassy of India in Abu Dhabi and the Consulate General of India in Dubai and the Northern Emirates have advised Indian nationals travelling to or residing in the UAE to take adequate medical insurance. In a joint advisory issued on 27 October, the Indian mission and post said they had received several instances of Indian nationals facing unforeseen illnesses or medical emergencies. These incidents resulted in huge medical bills beyond the capacity of patients or their family members to bear, due to inadequate insurance cover.All Indian nationals travelling to the UAE for visits or tourism have thus been advised to take adequate and appropriate medical insurance before commencing their journey. The insurance should also cover cashless facilities, including the cost of medical repatriation to India in the event of an unforeseen medical emergency.Indians residing in the UAE on employment visas or as dependents have also been advised to verify that their medical insurance is adequate to cover all medical expenses in the UAE and medical repatriation to India, in the event of emergency.

The India Meteorological Centre (IMD) has said that a well marked low pressure area over Eastcentral and adjoining Southeast Bay of Bengal persisted over the region today.It is most likely to persist over the region and intensify into a depression today. It is very likely to move west-northwestwards and intensify further into a deep depression tomorrow and into a cyclonic storm over the Westcentral Bay of Bengal by Monday morning.Under the influence of likely formation of cyclonic storm over the Westcentral Bay of Bengal by Monday and its further intensification, isolated extremely heavy rainfall is expected  over Coastal Andhra Pradesh on Tuesday and Wednesday and  further over Odisha and Telangana on Wednesday.IMD has issued red colour warning for heavy to very heavy rainfall with isolated extremely heavy rainfall over Kerala, Mahe, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal tomorrow.The Met Department has forecast Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep and South Interior Karnataka will experience heavy rainfall tomorrow. The weather agency has said that thunderstorms accompanied with lightning and gusty winds is likely over East Madhya Pradesh, and Andhra Pradesh tomorrow.

. Indian women wrestlers Kajal Dhochak and Neelam Sirohi have stormed into the finals of the World Championships with impressive victories in their respective semi-final bouts. Kajal defeated three-time World Championships medallist Aiperi Medet Kyzy of Kyrgyzstan, 10-7, in the women’s 76-kilogram category, making a remarkable comeback from a 1-7 deficit.Neelam secured a 7-3 victory over reigning Asian Games medallist Zeinep Bayanovа from Kazakhstan in the 50-kilogram semi-final. Both wrestlers have created history by reaching the World Championships finals, marking a significant achievement for Indian women’s wrestling.

. Cyclone Arnab has weakened after making landfall along the Andhra Pradesh-Yanam coast, but its impact continues to be felt across southern Odisha. The India Meteorological Department has forecast heavy to extremely heavy rainfall, strong winds and possible flash floods in several southern districts. Train services have been disrupted, while bus connectivity between Bhubaneswar and southern Odisha has also faced precautionary restrictions. The next 24 hours remain crucial for flood monitoring, public safety and restoration of essential services across the affected districts.“In Odisha, the immediate concern is the possibility of flash floods and waterlogging following intense rainfall associated with Cyclone Arnab. As the cyclone completed its landfall near Yanam this morning and weakened into a severe cyclonic storm, the IMD said it will weaken further into a deep depression by this evening and cross Malkangiri in Odisha. Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput and Malkangiri are among the districts facing significant rainfall and flash-flood risks. Nabarangpur is also experiencing heavy rainfall. IMD has warned of strong winds, with gusts potentially reaching eighty kilometres per hour in southern districts. Some northern districts will also have heavy rain with strong winds. The sea remains dangerous, and fishermen have been advised not to venture out. Railway services have been cancelled or regulated as a precaution, while bus services to southern Odisha have faced disruption. The state government has kept rescue teams ready, arranged shelters and directed officials to protect vulnerable residents and restore essential services. The next twenty-four hours are critical for Odisha. Even as the cyclone weakens, accumulated rainfall, swollen streams and sudden flooding may pose serious risks.

. India and Canada today held the inaugural meeting of the India-Canada Migration and Mobility Dialogue in New Delhi. The meeting was co-chaired by Secretary (Consular, Passport, Visa and Overseas Indian Affairs) in the External Affairs Ministry Sripriya Ranganathan and Deputy Minister of Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship of Canada, Ted Gallivan.During the meeting, the two sides signed the Terms of Reference for the Dialogue and reaffirmed their shared conviction that people are the strongest bridge between India and Canada. Discussions also focused on the mobility of students, skilled workers, professionals and business visitors as well as cooperation on migration management. The next meeting of the dialogue will be held in Canada.

. UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan has conferred the First Class Order of Zayed II on the flydubai crew members, including Captain Smit Machchhar. The honour, one of the UAE’s top civilian awards, has been conferred in recognition of their courageous efforts to ensure the safety of passengers during an in-flight incident aboard FZ1073, travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv on September 30.The UAE President, in the presence of Vice President & Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, received the crew members. The leaders praised the crew’s courage and professionalism in ensuring the safety of passengers and securing the aircraft, affirming that protecting people’s safety and security remains a top priority for the UAE. The crew members expressed their gratitude to the UAE President and pride in receiving the honour, which reflects recognition of their service, dedication and commitment.The honours were presented by UAE Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Defence, Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, who commended the crew’s actions and sense of responsibility. The ceremony was also attended by Sheikh Theyab bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, Deputy Chairman of the Presidential Court for Development and Fallen Heroes’ Affairs, and Sheikh Ahmed bin Saeed Al Maktoum, Chairman of Dubai Airports and Emirates Airline and Group, along with other senior officials.On September 30, Captain Smit Machchhar was attacked by his co-pilot while aboard flydubai flight FZ1073 enroute from Dubai to Tel Aviv. The crew, assisted by another pilot on board and passengers, intervened to bring the situation under control. The pilots regained control of the aircraft and diverted it to Tabuk in Saudi Arabia, where it landed safely. UAE investigations later revealed that the co-pilot had planned to seize the aircraft and carry out an attack at Tel Aviv airport.

. Major Asian stock indices displayed a mixed trend today. South Korea’s Kospi surged 3.1 per cent, outperforming its regional peers as a rise in semiconductor stocks and better economic data boosted investor sentiment. Japan’s Nikkei 225 gained 1.7 per cent, and Taiwan’s Taiex index rose marginally by 0.1 per cent. In contrast, China’s Shanghai Composite fell over 1.3 per cent, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng dropped 0.7 per cent, and Singapore’s Strait Times dipped more than 0.3 per cent.On the economic front, South Korea’s economy expanded by one per cent quarter-on-quarter in the third quarter of 2026, accelerating from 0.6 per cent in the previous quarter. On a year-on-year basis, GDP grew by 3.4 per cent according to the Bank of Korea’s advance estimate. Increased investment and exports, particularly of semiconductors, machinery and electrical equipment, were key contributors to growth.In European markets, Germany’s DAX climbed 0.4 per cent, while London’s FTSE 100 dipped 0.6 per cent, when reports last came in.

. The third season of the Nepal Premier League, Nepal’s premier franchise-based T20 cricket tournament, begins today at the Tribhuvan University International Cricket Ground in Kirtipur. The tournament will continue until November 21, with eight franchises competing for the title. The opening match will see defending champions Lumbini Lions take on last season’s runners-up, Sudurpaschim Royals. This season marks a major milestone, with International Cricket Council recognition and the introduction of the Decision Review System, allowing teams to challenge certain umpiring decisions. The tournament will feature international stars, including former Australian captain David Warner, West Indies all-rounder Andre Russell, South African batter David Miller and Bangladesh all-rounder Shakib Al Hasan.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices ended on a flat note today. The Sensex dropped eight points to close at 73,599. The Nifty slipped by three points to settle at 22,750.The broader market on the National Stock Exchange outperformed the frontline indices. The Midcap 100 index advanced one per cent, while the Smallcap 100 index jumped 2.7 per cent.In the Sensex pack, 18 out of 30 constituent companies registered gains. Among the top performers, Bharti Airtel rose 3.2 per cent, Trent gained 2.4 per cent, and Maruti advanced 2.3 per cent. In contrast, SBI as well as Axis Bank dropped over one and a half per cent, TCS slipped over 1.4 per cent, and Asian Paints fell by 1.4 per cent.In the sectoral indices on the BSE, 20 out of 28 sectors ended in the positive territory. Among the top movers, Healthcare rose almost 2.3 per cent, Telecommunication gained over 2.1 per cent, and Utilities advanced 1.9 per cent. Conversely, Top 10 Banks shed one per cent, Private Banks lost 0.8 per cent, and Bankex declined 0.7 per cent.The overall market breadth at the BSE was positive, as shares of 2,946 companies advanced, 1,370 declined and 231 remained unchanged.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has completed 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives. Today, in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into action through initiatives aimed at removing the colonial mindset.The history of modern India is deeply entangled with two centuries of British colonialism, and decades after Independence. Over the past few years, the Government has slowly been steering India, away from these vestiges of British rule. Addressing the nation from the Red Fort on the 76th Independence Day in 2022, the Prime Minister outlined five resolutions, or Panch Pran for the next 25 years. Elaborating on the second Praan, he said, in no part of citizens’ existence, not even in the deepest corners of mind or habits should there be any ounce of slavery.In a concerted effort to free the country from its colonial legacy and promote a distinct Indian identity, the Government has undertaken a series of initiatives across various sectors. the historic Rajpath in New Delhi was renamed Kartavya Path and inaugurated by the Prime Minister in 2022.  Similarly, a grand statue of freedom fighter Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose was installed near India Gate, which has replaced the statue of King George the Fifth. The Indian Navy also adopted a new ensign in 2022, replacing the earlier design that featured the Saint George’s Cross. The Government has merged the Rail Budget with the Union Budget from budget year 2017-18, ending a practice dating back to 1924. BJP leader Ram Madhav has said that restoring India’s cultural and civilizational identity is a symbol of self-respect. He added that decolonisation is the real patriotism that is happening today.The Government has further sought to revive literature banned during British rule, with the National Archives of India compiling a catalogue of banned poems, writings and publications from the freedom struggle. In addition, more than 1,500 obsolete laws have been repealed in recent years as part of efforts to simplify governance and remove outdated legal provisions.These initiatives reflect the Government’s stated commitment to building a confident, self-reliant India rooted in its cultural heritage and national values.

. The 9th Hero Hockey Men’s Asian Champions Trophy 2026 began at Jalandhar’s Olympian Surjit Hockey Stadium yesterday, with India routing Bangladesh by 13-0. This is the biggest win for India against the neighbouring country in the Asian Championship.Right from the first strike of the match till the end, India dominated all four quarters to win, with Capt Harmanpreet Singh leading from the front. He converted 2 penalty corners into goals, and others stood their ground to make no mistake in field goals. Mandeep Singh made a hat-trick; Dilpreet Singh and Hardik Singh each struck twice.Although some field strikes did not materialise, the host India hammered Bangladesh in its first match of the championship.Earlier, in the first two matches played during the day, Malaysia beat China by 5-4, whereas Japan defeated Korea by 3-2.Today is a rest day. On Thursday, October 29th, India will take on China, and Malaysia will play against South Korea, whereas Bangladesh will face Japan.Akashvani’s all-FM Rainbow Channels, along with Jalandhar’s Primary Channel, are broadcasting live commentary of matches played between India and other teams. The commentary of the semi-finals and final will also be available on these channels as well.

. In the forex market today, the rupee appreciated by seven paise to close at Rs 95.12 against the US dollar.The dollar index, which indicates US dollar’s strength against a basket of six other leading currencies, was trading at 102.18 in intra-day trade.

. In view of Cyclonic Storm Arnab, the Civil Aviation Ministry has reviewed the situation and taken measures to ensure aviation safety. The Ministry noted that flights to and from coastal Andhra Pradesh and southern Odisha are expected to be most affected. Hyderabad, Varanasi, Prayagraj and Gorakhpur may also witness knock-on delays depending on the storm’s track. The Ministry informed that airport operations at Visakhapatnam have remained suspended since yesterday afternoon. At Vijayawada and Rajahmundry, all flights were suspended after 7 PM yesterday. The Delhi-Bhogapuram-Delhi service also stands cancelled today.The Ministry updated that several flights remain cancelled. Six Air India flights on the Delhi-Visakhapatnam-Delhi route yesterday and the Delhi-Vijayawada-Delhi route today have been cancelled. Air India Express has also cancelled 13 flights, mostly involving Visakhapatnam services to and from Hyderabad, Bengaluru and Vijayawada, in addition to the Varanasi-Bangkok and Bangkok-Visakhapatnam services. Indigo has also suspended all flights at Visakhapatnam.The Ministry noted that the airlines have been advised to adhere to operational guidelines regarding adverse weather, inform passengers about delays and cancellations, and comply with applicable norms for rebooking and refunds. Passengers have also been advised to check their flight status on the airline’s website, app, helpline or through SMS before leaving for the airport.

Voting is underway across Israel in a high-stakes parliamentary election, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu facing a strong challenge from former military chief Gadi Eisenkot and other opposition leaders.  Over seventy-three lakh thirty one thousand voters are expected to cast their ballots to elect the 26th Knesset, Israel’s parliament. Polling stations opened at 9:30 am Indian Standard Time, and are scheduled to remain open until 12:30 am IST tonight.Exit polls are expected to provide the first indication of the election outcome shortly after voting ends. After the ballots are counted, the final results are expected to become available by 30th of this month with the results scheduled to be formally published on 4th of November.The election comes amid mounting scrutiny of Prime Minister Netanyahu’s leadership following the Hamas-led October 7 attack in 2023 and the wars that followed. 77 year old Netanyahu has served as Israel’s Prime Minister for more than 19 years across several terms. He is seeking to retain power as opposition leaders focus their campaigns on national security, accountability and the government’s handling of the failures surrounding the October 7 attack.Former Israel Defense Forces chief of staff Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party and one of Netanyahu’s main challengers in his campaign has portrayed Prime Minister Netanyahu’s continued leadership as a threat to Israel’s security, arguing that a change of government is necessary to restore public trust and ensure accountability. Mr Netanyahu, meanwhile, has sought to shift the focus towards the political makeup of a possible opposition-led government. The prime minister has portrayed his rivals as a left-leaning bloc that could depend on Arab parties to secure a parliamentary majority.Israel follows a system of proportional representation, under which voters choose political parties rather than directly electing a Prime Minister. The Knesset, Israel’s parliament, has 120 seats. A party or coalition therefore needs the support of at least 61 lawmakers to secure a parliamentary majority. Political parties must receive at least 3.25 per cent of the national vote to enter parliament. Seats are then allocated to qualifying parties broadly in proportion to their share of the vote.After the publication of results, Israeli President Isaac Herzog will then consult the leaders of the elected parties before deciding which lawmaker has the best chance of forming a government. The designated candidate will initially have 28 days to assemble a governing coalition, with a possible 14-day extension. The election outcome will determine whether Netanyahu can secure another term or whether the opposition can unite behind an alternative government.

In squash, India’s Anahat Singh has advanced to the quarterfinals of the Canadian Women’s Open squash tournament following a four-game victory over England’s Saran Nghiem.Currently ranked 15th in the world, Anahat defeated 52nd-ranked Saran 11-6, 4-11, 11-5, 11-7 in the second round. Anahat had received a bye in the first round. Anahat will now take on Egypt’s world No. 7 and top seed Fayrouz Aboelkheir in her next match.

. The Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has intensified action against misleading advertisements and non-compliant sale of walkie-talkies. The CCPA has imposed a penalty of one lakh rupees on a private company for misleading advertisements and product listings of walkie-talkies that failed to disclose essential regulatory information, including operating frequencies and applicable licensing requirements. The Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution said that the action forms part of the CCPA’s ongoing enforcement measures against misleading advertisements and unfair trade practices.It added that the CCPA had earlier taken suo motu cognisance of the large-scale listing and sale of walkie-talkies on e-commerce platforms without mandatory regulatory disclosures. During its examination, over sixteen thousand non-compliant listings were identified across platforms, and notices were issued to 13 e-commerce entities.The Ministry also informed that the Authority has so far passed final orders against 12 entities, imposing cumulative penalties of 58 lakh rupees for misleading advertisements and unfair trade practices relating to walkie-talkies.

Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) have remained net sellers of Indian equities, withdrawing 48,056 crore rupees in October so far amid elevated crude oil prices and escalating geopolitical tensions. However, last week they moderated their selling and turned net buyers on two trading days, signalling some easing in selling pressure.According to the latest depository data, of the total net outflows, 53,337 crore rupees were withdrawn through sales on stock exchanges. However, FPI investments through the primary market continued to witness inflows, amounting to 5,281 crore rupees so far this month.Meanwhile, the debt market has seen a mixed trend in Foreign Portfolio Investors’ flows during the period under review. FPIs have infused 3,737 crore rupees into debt securities through the General Limit route in October so far. In contrast, withdrawals from the Fully Accessible Route (FAR) stood at 3,858 crore rupees, while the Voluntary Retention Route (VRR) recorded outflows of 1,332 crore rupees.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said that India must innovate and lead the world in shaping the technologies of tomorrow. Speaking at the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave in New Delhi, Mr Modi said India must embrace the technologies of the future, innovate boldly and lead the world in creating them. He stressed that a Viksit Bharat will be built on strong foundations of scientific research, discoveries and the spirit of innovation. The Prime Minister stated that the nation is rapidly advancing its Fast Breeder Reactor technology. He highlighted that just a few months ago, the 500-Megawatt Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor successfully achieved first criticality.Mr Modi said that science truly succeeds when it steps out of the lab, improves the lives of common citizens, solves massive problems, and strengthens healthcare, agriculture, education, employment, and disaster resilience. He also highlighted that over the past year, the government has committed 12 thousand crore rupees to market-ready lab technologies, matched equally by 12 thousand crore rupees from private investors. He noted that annual patent filings have grown from fewer than 50,000 ten years ago to nearly 1.5 lakh last year, reflecting a deeper structural shift beyond mere numbers.Mr Modi said India aims to achieve self-reliance and build strength in critical technologies. He highlighted that the India of the 21st Century is moving ahead with a new mindset and newfound confidence. He stated that the goal is to create new technology for India, for the world, for today, and for the days to come.Meanwhile, Union Minister of State for Science and Technology Dr Jitendra Singh has said that India has established its position in science, innovation and technological capabilities, and the world is looking at the country with respect and admiration. He added that the international conference is witnessing enthusiastic participation, with thousands of experts and delegates joining the event on Indian soil.Prime Minister Modi also visited different sections of the exhibition and interacted with people. The exhibition includes around 150 deep-tech startup stalls, which will highlight technological developments and their potential applications across sectors.The three-day Conclave brings together leading scientists, researchers, academicians, policymakers, industry leaders, startups and international experts to deliberate on emerging technologies and India’s science, technology and innovation priorities. The deliberations will span 12 thematic areas, including artificial intelligence, biotechnology, advanced materials, manufacturing, healthcare, energy, climate and ocean sciences. Discussions will focus on research priorities, national capabilities and translating scientific advances into practical applications.

. Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports Mansukh Mandaviya has said that India will bring further amendments to the National Anti-Doping Act to introduce criminal provisions. He said the move is aimed at strengthening action against doping violations, including those involving coaches and supply chain stakeholders. Dr Mandaviya made the announcement while chairing the third formal meeting of the COP10 Bureau and the fourth formal meeting of the Fund’s Approval Committee for 2026-27 under the UNESCO International Convention against Doping in Sport in New Delhi.The Minister said sporting excellence must be accompanied by integrity and that athletes should compete on the basis of talent, preparation and hard work, rather than prohibited substances or methods. Highlighting the country’s efforts to combat doping, Dr Mandaviya said India has strengthened its legal and institutional framework through the National Anti-Doping Act, 2022, and its 2025 Amendment, both of which came into force in July 2026. He said the government plans to bring another amendment in the next session of Parliament to introduce criminal provisions to deal more effectively with violations, including those involving coaches and stakeholders in the supply chain. Dr. Mandaviya said the National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA) conducted more than 7,000 tests during 2025-26 and organised over 350 education and awareness sessions, reaching approximately 27,000 participants. The agency has also focused on risk-based testing and intelligence-led investigations to strengthen its efforts against doping.

. Vice President and Chairman of Rajya Sabha C. P. Radhakrishnan today met the Russian parliamentary delegation led by the Chairman of the State Duma of the Federal Assembly of Russia, Vyacheslav Volodin in New Delhi. The Vice President also extended his congratulations on the successful conduct of the election of deputies to the ninth convocation of the State Duma in the previous month.During the meeting, Mr Radhakrishnan expressed firm confidence that both countries will achieve the bilateral trade target of 100 billion dollar in annual trade by 2030, as agreed upon by the leadership of both nations. Mr Radhakrishnan also identified inter-regional cooperation, science and technology, cultural exchanges, and people-to-people ties as other vital areas of ongoing cooperation. Mr Radhakrishnan said that such discussions play a vital role in understanding mutual priorities, sharing experiences, and exploring actionable avenues for collaboration. He further reaffirmed the commitment to further strengthening ties for the mutual benefit of the people of both nations.Referring to key pillars of bilateral cooperation, the Chairman noted that preparations are currently underway for the 80th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between India and Russia. He expressed gratitude to Russia for its continued support toward the joint resolve of both nations in countering terrorism.On the occasion, Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha, Harivansh was also present.

. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh today held a meeting with US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth on the sidelines of the 13th ASEAN Defence Ministers’ Meeting (ADMM)-Plus in the Philippines. In a social media post, Mr Singh said that they had reviewed the progress of the 10-year India-US Defence Framework, driving strategic convergence across military technology, information sharing, and co-production. He said that the robust partnership of both nations continues to be a cornerstone for a free, open, and secure Indo-Pacific.

. A localised ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine took effect in the early hours today in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky, ahead of a planned humanitarian mission led by US First Lady Melania Trump. The truce is intended to allow aid deliveries to the city, where up to 2,000 people are reportedly facing severe shortages of food and medical supplies.However, Russian missile attacks continued in other parts of Ukraine, including Kyiv, highlighting the fragile nature of the ceasefire.Meanwhile, Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre held telephonic talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin to discuss the war and possible future negotiations involving Russia, Ukraine and the United States. The two Nordic leaders later spoke with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.The ceasefire comes amid renewed diplomatic efforts to ease the conflict, as civilians in affected areas continue to face worsening humanitarian conditions.Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov today said, Moscow has received no reports of violations of the local ceasefire.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi has completed 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues.Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives.Today, in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into action through the FDI Policy.India’s foreign direct investment policy has undergone major reforms over the past decade, with the government liberalising sectoral rules to attract greater foreign investment into the country. The government has progressively liberalised FDI norms in key sectors, including defence, telecommunications, insurance and space. Foreign investment of up to 74 per cent is permitted in defence, 100 per cent in telecom, insurance and Space sector. The country has received a record over 748 billion US dollars in FDI between 2014 and 2025. The number of source countries investing in India also rose from 89 to 112. Addressing the Rozgar Mela in New Delhi, Prime Minister Narendra Modi highlighted that today more than one hundred countries are investing in India through FDI.Chief Economic Advisor V. Anantha Nageswaran said that India has opened up several sectors, including space, drones, defence and insurance, to foreign investment.The FDI policy reforms reflect India’s efforts to create a more investor-friendly environment, simplified investment procedures and to strengthen its position as a preferred global investment destination.

. India and Mexico have taken a significant step towards strengthening their economic partnership with the signing of the Terms of Reference for a Preferential Trade Agreement. The signing formally marks the launch of negotiations for a mutually beneficial and balanced agreement aimed at expanding bilateral trade, creating new business opportunities, boosting investment flows, and building resilient and diversified supply chains. The Terms of Reference were signed by Commerce Secretary, Rajesh Agrawal, and Mexico’s Undersecretary of Foreign Trade, Luis Rosendo Gutiérrez Romano, in Mexico. The framework outlines key areas for negotiation, including market access for goods, rules of origin, customs procedures and trade facilitation, dispute settlement and technical barriers to trade.The initiative follows the understanding reached between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and President Claudia Sheinbaum during their meeting on the sidelines of the G7 Summit in Canada in June last year. During the meeting, the two leaders had agreed to further strengthen and deepen the India-Mexico partnership.

. Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal today met with the Hereditary Prince of Liechtenstein, Alois, in New Delhi today. In a social media post, Mr Goyal said that the discussions focused on further strengthening India-Liechtenstein economic and trade ties, including enhanced cooperation under the India-EFTA Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement (TEPA). He noted that the 100 billion dollar investment commitment under the India-EFTA TEPA reflects the shared ambition to deepen investment linkages, drive growth, and create big opportunities for businesses. Mr Goyal also highlighted India’s sustained efforts to create an investor-friendly business environment through reforms to enhance Ease of Doing Business.

. Very Severe Cyclonic Storm Arnab has completed its landfall along the Andhra Pradesh coast. The India Meteorological Department said the storm crossed the coast between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, near Narsapur and southwest of Yanam, between 2 AM and 8 AM today. At the time of landfall, the cyclone brought maximum sustained winds of 125 to 135 kilometres per hour, with gusts reaching 150 kilometres per hour. The landfall process was completed by 8 AM, with the storm’s central region moving entirely over land. As of 8:30 AM, the system was centred over coastal Andhra Pradesh and Yanam, near Narsapur. It is likely to move north-northwestwards and gradually weaken. The IMD expects it to weaken into a cyclonic storm within the next six hours and further into a deep depression during the following six hours.

. In Men’s Cricket, India defeated hosts New Zealand by six wickets in the third T-20 International at Wellington today, taking an unassailable three-nil lead in the five-match series. Chasing a target of 199 runs, India stormed to victory in just 13-point-two overs, losing four wickets. Abhishek Sharma led the charge with a sensational 113 off just 38 balls, while his opening partner, Vaibhav Suryavanshi, smashed a quickfire 45 off 19 deliveries.Earlier, New Zealand posted 198 for the loss of three wickets in their stipulated 20 overs. Daryl Mitchell finished unbeaten on 89 of 52 balls, while Finn Allen contributed 40. Arshdeep Singh, Axar Patel and Nitish Reddy claimed one wicket each for India. Abhishek Sharma was named Player of the Match for his match-winning knock.

. Indian Railways has announced 1,265 vacancies for Station Master posts across various Railway Recruitment Boards and zones, opening up new employment opportunities for graduate candidates. The Railways Ministry said that in an important recruitment-related decision, the Railway Board has prescribed that Station Master recruitment will be notified separately from 2026 onwards. The dedicated recruitment process provides candidates with a specific notification covering eligibility requirements, examination procedures and vacancy distribution for the post. The online application window will remain open till 25th of next month. Candidates are advised to review the detailed eligibility conditions, vacancy distribution and application instructions before submitting their forms. The recruitment reflects Indian Railways’ continued efforts to provide career opportunities to eligible candidates while strengthening its operational workforce.

. India stormed into the semifinals of the inaugural Commonwealth Kabaddi Championship with a 48-20 win over Tanzania in Ahmedabad yesterday, extending their unbeaten run to five matches. The semifinal is scheduled for Friday. India, assured of a top finish in the group stage, have one match remaining against Sri Lanka tomorrow.In the women’s competition, Kenya defeated Scotland 61-16 to maintain their unbeaten run, while Malaysia thrashed Singapore 62-17. Elsewhere, Bangladesh beat Singapore 60-28, with Mijanur Rahman scoring 12 points and Dipayon Golder contributing 10 points. Canada defeated Scotland 62-30 for their second win of the tournament, with Anmol Thakur and Manpreet Singh scoring 19 and 15 points, respectively.

Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives. Today, in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into action through initiatives like Give It Up Campaign.The Give It Up campaign, launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in 2015, has encouraged consumers to voluntarily give up their LPG subsidies. Under the campaign, more than one crore 13 lakh LPG consumers have voluntarily surrendered their LPG subsidy. The savings helped provide LPG connections to poor households under the Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana, particularly benefiting rural women who relied on firewood and cow dung for cooking. The government has provided over ten crore 56 lakh free LPG connections under the scheme to adult women from poor households across the country. Addressing the Delhi Economics Conclave in 2015, Prime Minister Modi highlighted that the Give It Up movement inspired the citizens to come together to help underprivileged families acquire clean fuel.A resident of Uttar Pradesh, Sanju Devi said that the gas stove has made cooking much more convenient and freed her from exposure to smoke.The Give It Up campaign has promoted a sense of social responsibility among citizens and has supported the government’s efforts to ensure clean cooking fuel access for all.

. Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal has said India plans to increase its port capacity fourfold by 2047 to support economic growth andexpandinginternational trade. Speaking in Rotterdam during his visit to the Netherlands, Mr Goyal said, India had doubled its port capacity over the past decade and aims to quadruple it over the next two decades. He highlighted opportunities for cooperation with the Port of Rotterdam in the Netherlands in maritime infrastructure, green energy, carbon capture and sustainable trade.The Minister emphasised the importance of cooperation with the Port of Rotterdam in modernising existing ports, developing world-class infrastructure and improving operational efficiency. Highlighting the government’s Sagarmala initiative, the Minister said efforts were underway to expand port infrastructure and improve maritime connectivity.The Minister expressed confidence that stronger cooperation with major international maritime hubs such as Rotterdam would help India expand its maritime capabilities and strengthen its role in global trade.Describing India as the world’s fastest-growing major economy, Mr Goyal said the country had made significant progress in quality, efficiency and productivity, strengthening its position in global trade and logistics.

. In the Indian bullion market today, 24 carat gold dropped nearly 0.2 per cent to 1,41,431 rupees per 10 grams. Silver was one per cent down at 1,92,499 rupees per kilogram, according to the closing rates from the India Bullion and Jewellers Association.

. The parliamentary election in Israel remained deadlocked, with exit polls from all three major television networks giving opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot’s bloc a narrow two-seat lead over Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s camp. The projections put Eisenkot’s bloc at 52 seats and Netanyahu’s Likud-led alliance at 50, leaving neither side with the 61 seats needed for a majority in the 120-member parliament – Knesset.The results could give Eisenkot the first chance to form a government, but his path to power remains uncertain. The remaining 18 seats were projected to go to Arab parties not aligned with either bloc, and Eisenkot has largely ruled out forming a government with them. Netanyahu, meanwhile, could remain caretaker prime minister if coalition talks fail.Israel’s Central Elections Committee said voter turnout reached 77.7%, the highest in more than two decades and around seven percentage points above the 2022 election. The vote was the first since the Hamas-led October 7, 2023, attacks and the ensuing wars in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran.Netanyahu has served as prime minister for nearly 19 of the past 30 years and has repeatedly survived political crises. His opponents removed him from office only once since 2009, but he returned to power 18 months later.With the latest exit polls showing a narrow advantage for Eisenkot’s bloc but no clear majority for either side, the final count and subsequent coalition negotiations will determine who can form Israel’s next government.

. In Tennis, India’s top-ranked doubles player, Yuki Bhambri, with his American partner Ryan Seggerman, clinched the Almaty Open title in Kazakhstan today. The fourth-seeded Indo-American pair defeated top seeds Lucas Miedler and Neil Oberleitner of Austria 7-6, 6-7, 10-2 in the final of ATP 250 tournament. The victory marks Bhambri’s first ATP Tour title of the 2026 season and the fifth doubles title of his career on the ATP Tour. The 34-year-old had previously won ATP 250 titles in Mallorca in 2023, Gstaad and Munich in 2024, and the ATP 500 Dubai tournament in 2025.

. The International Weightlifting Federation (IWF) today announced that Ahmedabad will host the Senior World Weightlifting Championships in 2029. This will be the first time that India hosts the senior edition of the prestigious global event. The decision was taken at the IWF Executive Board meeting held in Ningbo, China. The IWF also awarded the hosting rights for the 2030 Senior World Weightlifting Championships to Moscow, the capital of Russia. Additionally, the IWF Executive Board decided to award the hosting rights for the 2028 World Youth Championships to Prishtina, Kosovo, and the World Junior Championships to Caracas, Venezuela.

. Bangladesh’s dengue death toll has reached 400 this year, with 11 more fatalities reported in the 24 hours until yesterday morning, marking the highest single-day toll recorded so far in 2026. According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), 2,071 new infections were reported, taking the total number of cases to 128,237. Currently, 6,415 patients are receiving treatment in hospitals nationwide, while 121,422 have recovered.Meanwhile, Bangladesh has reported seven more deaths among children with confirmed measles or measles-like symptoms, bringing the combined toll to 1,240 this year.The DGHS classified six of the latest fatalities as suspected measles deaths and one as confirmed. The country has recorded 105 confirmed measles deaths and 1,135 suspected deaths.Authorities also reported 1,232 new suspected measles cases and 63 laboratory-confirmed infections in the latest 24-hour period. Cumulative suspected cases have reached 223,784, while confirmed infections stand at 23,541.The figures highlight the continuing public health challenges posed by dengue and measles in Bangladesh.

. India’s Aditya has won the gold medal at the World Under-19 Boxing Championships in Montenegro. Aditya defeated Russia’s Islam Magomedov by a 4-1 margin in the men’s 55-kilogram final to claim the world title. This is India’s first gold medal of this edition of the U19 World Boxing Championships.India’s Harshika won bronze in the women’s 65-kilogram category, while Prachi Tokas secured a bronze medal in the women’s over-80-kilogram category.India’s Megha Sheokand will face Russia’s Ekaterina Frolova in the women’s 80-kilogram final later tonight.
